complexity_scope.guarantee: Uniform instancewise failure probability at most delta in the quantile definition; not expectation.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: Positive constants depend only on p.
complexity_scope.oracle: Fresh unbiased stochastic subgradient kernel under both conditional centered moment bounds; exact known prox free; unknown values and reusable random functions unavailable.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Feasible point xhat; minimax objective-error quantile E_T^(mu)(delta).
complexity_scope.regime: All integer budgets T>=1 and 0<delta<1/10; upper every finite d, lower d>=ceil(L^2/s^2).
complexity_scope.resource: Total raw stochastic calls T including every rejected sample; deterministic internal computation uncharged.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Existence upper bound with unrestricted internal computation; lower covers all adaptive randomized algorithms with arbitrary feasible outputs and at most T raw calls almost surely.

content.intended_use: Retain saturation, initialization and curvature while distinguishing unmatched deterministic transients.

proofs.locator: Appendix A.1–A.3, B.1–B.2, C.1–C.4 and D.1–D.3, printed pages 13–21
map: Import Lemma A.3: conditional average regret for fixed comparator in radius-R ball is at most C_p R[(M+sqrt(V))/sqrt(n)+M log(3/alpha)/n+s0(log(3/alpha)/n)^q]. Appendix A proves the scalar clipping/Gaussian estimate and density-entropy mirror argument; these are source interfaces, not separate batch lemmas.

Appendix B.1 realizes virtual decisions using only prox_h: project the raw subgradient onto the affine-hull translation space, query a nearby relative-interior point, and add a predictable correction. The mean norm is <=4G, centered moments are preserved, and equation (25) transfers regret to objective gap with GR/(2n) error.

Lemma B.1 controls conditional rejection: for tau>=64(4G+L), rejection <=1/16, bias <=C_p s(L/tau)^(p-1), accepted centered second moment <=C_p L^p tau^(2-p), and directional moment <=C_p s^p. Proposition B.2 couples ideal accepted draws to a cap of 4n raw calls. Exhaustion probability <=2^(-8n); no concentration conditional on completion is used.

Appendix C gives the free proximal cap H(G), convex primitive, and strong-convexity localization. Radii halve; backwards failure allocation delta_j=delta 2^(j-J-1) and Lemma C.1 sum the budgets without an additional horizon logarithm. Threshold tau=128 max{4G+L,L(T/e)^(1/p)} yields v_T. Procedure selection uses public parameters rather than unknown objective values.

Appendix D uses f_v(x)=(a/sqrt(k)) sum_{j<=k}|x_j-rho v_j|, rho=R_a/sqrt(k), R_a=D for mu=0 and min{D,a/mu} otherwise, with common quadratic r. Wrong decoded signs cost H(a)/k. Gaussian, independently masked-coordinate, and one-coordinate erasure kernels force respectively min{G,L/sqrt(T)}, min{G,A/T^q}, and min{G,s(ell/T)^q}. Their conditional centered moment membership, adaptive transcript controls and quantile conversion are supplied in D.2–D.3.

Take the maximum of the three lower components and use equation (8), c^2 H(a)<=H(ca)<=c H(a) for 0<=c<=1, with K^q comparable to e^q+ell^q. At atoms use a strictly smaller threshold, as stated at the end of Appendix D.
proofs.omitted_details: Long literature proof is imported through the explicitly located interfaces; it is not independently reproved or fully transcribed. External literature results are not separately verified.
proofs.reading_coverage: Main definitions and statements visually checked on native pages 4–6; Appendix A–D relevant proof text read directly from original PDF extraction.

assumptions: X is a known nonempty closed convex subset of R^d. Unknown f is convex and G-Lipschitz on X. Known r is convex and mu-strongly convex on X; mu=0 allows arbitrary convex r, including r=0. h=r+indicator_X is proper, closed and convex, and exact prox_{eta h} is available for every eta>0.
F=f+r attains a minimum at x*. A supplied feasible x1 has ||x1-x*||<=D. The domain can be unbounded and the objective nonsmooth.

At query x in X a fixed query-dependent kernel returns g(x,xi) with mean in partial f(x). Each call is fresh and independent of prior history conditional on its query; repeated frozen-query calls are independent kernel copies.

For each raw call t, conditionally on preceding history, zeta_t=g_t-E_{t-1}g_t satisfies E_{t-1}||zeta_t||^p<=L^p and sup_{||v||=1} E_{t-1}|<v,zeta_t>|^p<=s^p. These are separate assumptions; a small s is not implied by knowing L.

Function values and reusable random sample functions are unavailable. Known-set/regularizer deterministic operations and exact prox are uncharged. Public inputs include G,D,L,s,p,mu,T,delta,X,r; internal computation is unrestricted.
Upper bound holds for every finite dimension. Lower bound additionally requires d>=ceil(e).
statement.conclusion: c_p H(min{G,w_T}) <= E_T^(mu)(delta) <= C_p H(min{G,v_T}). For mu=0 this is c_p D min{G,w_T} <= E_T^(0)(delta) <= C_p D min{G,v_T}. For mu>0 it implies E_T^(mu)(delta) <= (C_p/mu)[(G^2+L^2)/T+G^2 ell^2/T^2+(A^2+s^2 ell^(2q))/T^(2q)]. The envelope can be sharper than this expansion. G/sqrt(T) and G ell/T occur only in the upper amplitude; their presence does not establish matching deterministic finite-budget complexity.
statement.objects_and_definitions: All norms are Euclidean. Let J_mu be the model class specified in assumptions and A_T the adaptive randomized algorithms using at most T raw calls almost surely. Define E_T^(mu)(delta)=inf_{A in A_T} inf{epsilon>=0: sup_{I in J_mu} P_I(F_I(xhat_A)-min F_I>epsilon)<=delta}. Probability includes oracle and internal algorithm randomness. Set q=1-1/p, e=L^2/s^2, A=s e^q, ell=log(3/delta), K=e+ell, w_T=L/sqrt(T)+s(K/T)^q, v_T=G/sqrt(T)+G ell/T+w_T. H(a)=max_{0<=rho<=D}(a rho-mu rho^2/2): H(a)=Da if mu=0; H(a)=a^2/(2mu) if mu>0 and a<=mu D; H(a)=Da-mu D^2/2 if mu>0 and a>=mu D.
statement.parameter_domains: 1<p<=2; G,D>0; 0<s<=L; mu>=0; finite integer d>=1; integer T>=1; 0<delta<1/10.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every admissible public parameter tuple, integer T>=1 and 0<delta<1/10, there exist positive c_p,C_p depending only on p with the displayed bounds. The upper witness is an admissible algorithm selected from public-parameter bounds. The lower bound covers every adaptive randomized algorithm, including arbitrary feasible output and almost-sure early stopping, and is witnessed by instances with X=R^d and common known r(x)=mu||x||^2/2.

summary: A two-sided envelope for minimax quantile risk, with statistical amplitude in the lower bound and additional deterministic transients in the upper bound; not unconditional all-budget matching.
